KEY MESSAGE 1...

A front loitering near the Virginia/North Carolina border could 
prompt a few showers or thunderstorms in southwest Virginia or far 
southeast West Virginia this afternoon. Showers and
thunderstorms are also possible in and near the mountains 
tonight into Tuesday, as a mid/upper-level short wave crosses, 
further encouraged by upslope southeast flow on the southeast 
side of the mountains tonight, in a moisture-rich modestly
unstable environment. This system is not to be confused with
that associated with a severe thunderstorms and heavy rainfall 
threat for Tuesday afternoon into Tuesday night, Key Message 
number 2. Otherwise, high pressure will provide dry conditions 
to the majority of the area today into Tuesday morning.

Smoke from distant Canadian wildfires should gradually diminish
today, as a residual layer of low-level east to northeast flow
this morning becomes south to southwest this afternoon, cutting
off the Canadian sources.

Temperatures and dew points will continue a little above normal
for mid Summer.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

Long wave trough in the east/ridge in the west pattern 
amplification via an embedded short-wave trough crossing the 
forecast and county warning area on Tuesday will drive a surface
cold front toward the area Tuesday afternoon and evening, and 
then on through the area overnight Tuesday night into Wednesday.

The trick of the tale to this forecast is the well defined
embedded short wave ahead of the surface cold front on Tuesday,
encouraging instability amid the midday heating in the moisture
rich, high shear environment. The associated 0-6 band 0-8 km 
shear of 40 to 60 kts will encourage an area of organized 
convection that crosses Tuesday midday into the afternoon that 
will carry a damaging wind threat, as well as hail and a tornado
threat with more discrete cells or supercells.

The round of convection Tuesday midday into Tuesday afternoon
will leave behind a cool pool suppressing surface based 
instability for a time Tuesday afternoon. Driven by a more 
subtle embedded short wave driving the surface cold front toward
the area Tuesday evening, the strength of showers and 
thunderstorms ahead of the cold front Tuesday evening will 
depend upon how much the atmosphere can recover, but the high 
shear environment will encourage organization of convection 
into a line or line segments, giving rise to a second damaging 
wind threat Tuesday evening.

Furthermore, impressive low level flow for mid to late July, 40
to 50 kts at h85 and 30 to 40 kts at h925, contribute to 0-3 km
shear of 30 to 40 kts Tuesday afternoon and evening. With the 
help of low LCLs, this elevates the Significant Tornado 
Parameter above, even well above, 2 Tuesday evening, thus 
elevating the Tornado threat.

The strong flow through the column, veering in the low to mid
levels and at times in the mid to upper levels, gives rise to
curved hodographs throughout much of the Tuesday/Tuesday night 
period, with all three severe weather hazards, damaging wind, 
tornado and hail, at play to at least some degree during both 
rounds of convection.

The Storm Prediction Center has expanded the enhanced risk for 
severe thunderstorms southeastward, to now include nearly all of
the forecast and county warning area, with all three severe 
weather hazards at play Tuesday into Tuesday night. 

In addition, the rich moisture, with surface dew points in the
mid 70s F, h85 theta e values up to around 350 K and PW values 
up to around two inches, contributes to significant instability
as will as high rainfall rates. With multiple rounds of high 
coverage convection, flash flooding is likely to become an issue
wherever heavy rainfall is most persistent or repetitive.

The Weather Prediction Center has a slight risk for excessive 
rainfall throughout the forecast and county warning area for 
Tuesday and Tuesday night.

KEY MESSAGE 3...

Wednesday is likely to begin with fog and stratus, as the cold
front contributing to the severe weather threat on Tuesday
pushes out of the area to the southeast in the morning. Also,
showers and thunderstorms are still possible in and near the
mountains before the front pushes all the way through.

While a mid/upper-level trough lingers amid a trough in the
east/ridge in the west pattern, high pressure at the surface 
brings quieter weather for the conclusion of the work week.

An embedded mid/upper-level short wave trough will encourage 
the front southeast of the area to buckle back toward the area 
as well as an inverted trough in or just west of the mountains.
Similar to the pattern this afternoon and tonight, this may 
encourage showers and afternoon thunderstorms there Friday 
afternoon through the weekend.

Models are coming into better agreement on another cold front 
bringing the chance for showers and thunderstorms to the area 
next Monday afternoon into Monday night.
